questions.question: If a bus has a brake and accelerator interlock system, what should it do?

options.text: Be turned off in most situations.
Only be used in bad weather.
Never replace the parking brake.
Operate the rear door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never replace the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Some buses have a brake and accelerator interlock system. It applies the brakes and stops the engine when the rear door is open. This system should never be used instead of the parking brake.

questions.question: What is true about gasoline on a bus?

options.text: It can be brought onto a bus.
It can never be brought onto a bus.
It can be stored in the passenger area during long trips.
It should be stored in glass containers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can never be brought onto a bus.
questions.explanation: Drivers and passengers cannot bring hazardous items like gasoline or car batteries onto a bus.

questions.question: If a bus stalls on railroad tracks, what should the driver do?

options.text: Get everyone off the bus and move far away from the tracks.
Keep everyone on the bus and try to wave the train down.
Keep everyone on the bus and wait for help.
Keep everyone on the bus and call a tow truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get everyone off the bus and move far away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If a bus stalls on railroad tracks, the driver must evacuate everyone immediately. Lead passengers far away from the bus in the direction of any oncoming train to avoid debris from the collision.

questions.question: During a bus evacuation, students should be led at least ____ away from the road.

options.text: 10 feet
20 feet
50 feet
100 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: During an evacuation, lead students at least 100 feet away from the road in the direction of oncoming traffic. This protects them from debris if another vehicle hits the bus.

questions.question: If a driver is near a school with students present and has no helper, what can they do?

options.text: Back the vehicle.
Back the vehicle if the path looks clear.
Back the vehicle if going no faster than 10 mph.
Cannot back the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot back the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A bus cannot be backed up at a school when students are nearby unless a responsible person is there to guide the driver.

questions.question: What must a bus driver do regarding a seat belt?

options.text: Does not need to wear one.
Must always wear one.
Must wear one only during school hours.
Must wear one only if licensed for less than a year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always wear one.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must always wear a seat belt. The driver's seat should have a seat belt, and it must be used at all times.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, who decides whether to proceed?

options.text: Each driver decides.
A control device decides.
Surrounding vehicles decide.
Passengers in the vehicle decide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each driver decides.
questions.explanation: Passive railroad crossings have no traffic control devices. Each driver must decide if it is safe to cross by looking for trains themselves.

questions.question: Hazardous materials must be marked with all of the following except:

options.text: The material's name.
The material's identification number.
The appropriate hazard label.
The phone number of a contact person.

questions.correctAnswerText: The phone number of a contact person.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must show the material's name, identification number, and hazard label. Do not transport hazardous materials unless you are sure they are allowed.

questions.question: To keep passengers safe, what should a driver check?

options.text: Emergency exit handles.
Floor coverings.
Signaling devices.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before each trip, check the inside of the bus for safety. Make sure handholds, railings, signaling devices, floor coverings, and emergency exit handles all work properly.

questions.question: Where should carry-on bags be placed on a bus?

options.text: In front of the back door.
In front of the front door.
In a location that does not block emergency exits.
On top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a location that does not block emergency exits.
questions.explanation: Bags cannot be placed in doorways or aisles. Baggage must be secured so it does not damage the bus, allows the driver to move freely, lets passengers exit through any window or door in an emergency, and does not injure passengers if it falls.

questions.question: On a bus with outside convex mirrors, where are they located?

options.text: Below the outside flat mirrors.
Above the outside flat mirrors.
Next to the door.
On top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Below the outside flat mirrors.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, outside convex mirrors are placed below the outside flat mirrors. They help the driver see a wide area around the bus, including traffic, clearance, and students.

questions.question: When should a driver explain passenger comfort and safety rules?

options.text: At the beginning of the trip.
At the end of the trip.
Only if an issue arises.
Only if a passenger asks.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the beginning of the trip.
questions.explanation: Many bus carriers have rules about smoking, drinking, and using music players on the bus. Explaining safety and comfort rules at the start of the trip helps prevent problems later.

questions.question: Before driving a bus that has been parked for a few days, what should a driver do?

options.text: Assume the interior is in good condition.
Call the local police to inspect the bus.
Walk through the bus to check for damage since the last trip.
Ask passengers to check the interior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for damage since the last trip.
questions.explanation: Unattended buses can be damaged. Before each trip, the driver should check the inside of the bus to make sure all key systems work properly and riders are safe.

questions.question: What is an active railroad crossing?

options.text: A crossing with traffic control devices installed.
A crossing with no traffic control devices.
A crossing where at least 10 vehicles cross the tracks every hour.
A crossing that should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossing with traffic control devices installed.
questions.explanation: Active railroad crossings have traffic control devices such as flashing red lights, warning bells, and gates. Drivers must always follow the directions of these devices.

questions.question: How is student safety best maintained in an emergency?

options.text: Keep students on the bus.
Let some students leave while others stay.
Let all students evacuate the bus.
Create panic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep students on the bus.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safest when they stay on the bus and remain under control.

questions.question: Where should carry-on bags be placed on a bus?

options.text: In front of the back door.
In front of the front door.
Where everyone can reach all emergency exits.
On top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where everyone can reach all emergency exits.
questions.explanation: Bags must not block aisles or doors. All baggage must be placed so it does not get damaged, the driver can move freely, passengers can exit through any window or door in an emergency, and items cannot fall or hurt anyone.

questions.question: When should a driver announce passenger comfort rules like smoking guidelines?

options.text: Only if there is a rule violation.
Only if a passenger asks about something.
At the start of the trip.
To each passenger individually.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the start of the trip.
questions.explanation: Many bus carriers have rules about smoking, drinking, and music players. Announcing these rules at the start of the trip helps prevent problems later.

questions.question: A bus driver does not need to stop when approaching which of these?

options.text: A raised drawbridge.
A streetcar crossing.
A railroad crossing.
A stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A streetcar crossing.
questions.explanation: At railroad crossings, drivers must stop 15 to 50 feet from the tracks, look and listen for trains, and only proceed when certain no trains are coming. Drivers do not need to stop at streetcar crossings, when a police officer is directing traffic, when there is a green traffic signal, or at crossings marked 'exempt' or 'abandoned.'

questions.question: What does the overhead inside rearview mirror allow the driver to see?

options.text: What is happening inside the bus.
What is happening outside the bus.
Traffic monitoring.
Whether the door is open or closed.

questions.correctAnswerText: What is happening inside the bus.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, the overhead inside rearview mirror lets the driver watch what passengers are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: If you must back up at a student pick-up point, when should you back up?

options.text: Before the students board the bus.
After all students have boarded the bus.
After half the students board, then back toward the others.
Tell students to wait, then back toward the stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: After all students have boarded the bus.
questions.explanation: If you must back up a school bus at a student pick-up point, pick up all students first before backing up. When backing, watch for students who arrive late.
